Subject: Post-call: SLO tuning & model-paths — Shoplytics

Hi Rajiv / Alice,

Thanks again for the call — appreciate the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before the pilot kickoff.

Key SLOs you called out on the demo:
- P95 latency target: ~200ms (user-facing single-turn inference for product search ranking)
- Max sustained concurrency: 150 concurrent requests during promotional spikes
- Streaming: must support progressive ranking updates within a 2s overall window for the UI (partial results ok)
- Availability: tolerate regional fallback to lower-cost variants; 99.5% uptime target for pilot

Primary cost/perf levers we discussed that we'll evaluate for the pilot:
1) Continuous batching + dynamic batch sizing (prefer latency SLO-aware batching)
2) Prefix / KV caching for hot queries (30–40% cache hit expected on repeat searches)
3) Quantization profiles: int8 for standard queries, int4 for deep long-tail where quality delta acceptable
4) Model variants: ensemble of compact tuned model for high-concurrency, larger model for quality-critical flows with automatic routing

Initial asks (owner in parentheses):
- Redwood: produce a one-page pilot config with expected P95 and cost deltas for the levers above (Karthik, Ben) — deliver by Tue 16 Mar EOD
- Shoplytics: share 1 week of peak-hour anonymized logs (Alice) and any hard latency budget constraints from front-end teams (Rajiv)
- Procurement: high-level PO / procurement timeline so we can align billing/commitments (Rajiv)

Attachments: I attached a thin SLO playbook draft and a cost model template to populate.

Next meeting: propose Wed 17 Mar 10:00am PT to review the config and pick the pilot model-path. If that doesn't work, tell me a couple of slots.

Thanks —
Hannah

Thanks Hannah — that summary looks right. A couple of clarifications from our side before you build the config: 
1) For the streaming requirement, we actually need the first partial ranking within 300ms for the majority (we can accept re-ranks up to 2s). Can you model both the 300ms-first-byte and 2s-final-window scenarios?
2) Concurrency: we have existing backend queuing that will fan out; the 150 concurrent is an upper bound — realistically expect 60–100 sustained but spikes to 150 for promos. Please show both sustained and burst profiles in the cost model.

Procurement note: we can sign a 3-month pilot PO; Alice will confirm exact timing tomorrow.

Appreciate the speedy turnaround.

Rajiv / Hannah — attaching a short technical breakdown + preliminary cost model populated for the two streaming scenarios Rajiv requested. Attachments: slo_playbook_v2.pdf, cost-models-shoplytics.xlsx, latency-batching-chart.png

Summary of Karthik's analysis (quick bullets):
- 300ms-first-byte constraint: requires aggressive micro-batching with per-request prioritization and a compact model variant on GPUs with faster kernels. Estimated P95 achievable: ~280–320ms without KV cache; with 30% cache hit we estimate P95 ~180–220ms.
- 2s-final-window scenario: allows larger batches and a higher-quality model; P95 with compact+int8 quant is ~350–420ms single-node but overall UX within 2s when progressive streaming employed.
- Concurrency profiles: for sustained 80 QPS (expected sustained) we recommend 2 dedicated instances (reserved pool) + autoscale buffers for promo spikes to 150. For strict cost control we recommend a hybrid reserved+burst policy.
- Quantization split: int8 for production path (good quality/cost tradeoff); int4 for long-tail non-critical queries where we can accept a small quality delta. We'll include per-token cost delta in the sheet.

Pilot proposal:
- Phase 0 (week 1): ingest anonymized logs, run offline sim using our batching model to calibrate expected latency distribution.
- Phase 1 (weeks 2–4): live pilot on a subset of traffic (10–20%) using routing rules: compact-int8 for search baseline, large-int8 for result re-ranks; KV cache enabled for top 1k queries.
- Success criteria: meet 200ms P95 for cached flows and <2s final window for end-to-end streaming in 90% of sessions.

Next steps (Karthik): I will update the cost-models sheet with two columns: sustained and burst. Hannah: can you lock Wed 17 Mar 10am PT for a review?

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference
